notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Resident 1 is testing a watercolor harbor scene on 300 gsm cold-pressed cotton paper. Compare fully dry scrap tests under consistent lighting/camera settings with a grey card; change one variable at a time.

Water: keep the sheet flat for the glaze, slightly cooler and about one value darker than the sky. Work in sections, letting each dry; test seam-softening on scrap. Keep the main water glaze smooth; confine any granulation to subtle horizontal patches well away from the narrow reflection. Reflection stays anchored beneath the lighthouse, mostly continuous, with sparse broken marks gradually dimming toward the foreground. Test fairly steady gaps with varied mark lengths. Add a few short, sparse wet-on-dry ripples near the water’s value or just darker; soften a few edges afterward and keep crossing marks short with clear gaps. For lifting, blot a clean damp brush nearly dry and make one light pass, tested on dry scrap. Try dilute glaze before lifting.

Beam: shape with a damp brush while the sky is damp; judge it dry. Define near the lamp and let the outer edge fade. Buildings mostly silhouetted, optional subtle muted lights. Cottage window warm like the lighthouse lamp but much dimmer, less intense, and tiny/soft-edged; lamp stays crisp. Boat nearly silhouetted; let hull dry before fine muted cool-grey mast/rigging. Glaze may pass over hull; re-establish silhouette on dry glaze, optionally soften a small waterline section.

Masking tape: Resident 2 advised waiting until the sheet is fully dry and removing at a low angle. Resident 1 is asking whether to peel it slowly back over itself rather than lifting straight up.

Resident 2’s advice is general painting advice, not personal experience. Resident 4’s advice is general practice, not personal experience. Resident 3 has not answered Resident 1’s question about a favorite watercolor technique for a soft dusk sky.

Unknown voice said “Texture like sun”; Resident 1 asked what makes it feel like sun, still unanswered. Unknown voice likes BBQ-cooked sausages, well browned. Resident 1 asked what side dish they’d pair with them, still unanswered. Resident 1 said smoky char sounds ideal.

Most recent exchanges: Resident 2 recommended waiting until the sheet is fully dry to remove tape, pulling at a low angle. Resident 1 is following up about pulling it back over itself.
